newsitem.title: CANADA: Loram Corp considering spinoff of energy companies.
newsitem.headline: Loram Corp considering spinoff of energy companies.

text.p: Loram Corp, a private holding company owned by Calgary's Mannix family, said on Tuesday it was considering a spinoff of its coal mining and energy concerns in deals that would likely bring in proceeds of well over C$1 billion.

Loram said it retained RBC Dominion Securities to review its ownership of Manalta Coal Ltd, Canada's biggest coal producer, and Pembina Corp, a Calgary-based oil and gas producer and pipeline operator.

At a press conference on Tuesday, Ron and Fred Mannix and Loram Chief Executive Lorne Gordon told reporters that buoyant energy market conditions and strong demand for assets convinced Loram to examine such potential deals as income trust issues and outright sales for the firms.

"The companies are leaders in their fields and current positive market conditions suggest that there's a strong market for sound investment opportunities in quality companies like these," said Fred Mannix.
The review was expected to continue through August, the officials said.

They said no other Mannix investments, which include real estate holdings, railway maintenance and equipment manufacturing companies as well as other industrial interests, would be placed on the block.

Manalta, owned by the family for 60 years, produces 27 million tons per year of coal -- one third of Canada's annual output -- from eight mines in Alberta, British Columbia and Saskatchewan. Annual revenues are C$550 million, Gordon said.
Its spinoff would follow a similar deal last year, in which Alberta's Mitchell family placed the assets of Luscar Coal into a royalty trust valued at C$480 million.
Pembina, which the Mannix family has owned since 1954, produces 11,500 barrels of oil and gas liquids and 100 million cubic feet of natural gas per day in western Canada.

It is also Canada's largest owner and operator of oil and gas liquids feeder pipelines, which carry about 325,000 barrels a day to refineries and other lines in Edmonton from various parts of Alberta and British Columbia.
Pembina's yearly revenues total about C$300 million, Gordon said.
Employees at the two companies number 2,300.
Few other details were offered to reporters on Tuesday, including what Loram would do with the potential proceeds.
Gordon said Loram had been approached at various times to deal on the operations, but offers had always been rebuffed.
The Mannixes, known in Calgary for jeolously guarding their privacy, said both Manalta and Pembina were profitable and no outside interests were convincing the family to spin them off.
"This is a business decision taken on our own initiative, at a time of our own choosing and in pursuit of our own objectives," Ron Mannix said.
The family has operated business interests from its Calgary home base for about 100 years. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
